newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold volume slips as prices firm.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold volume slips as prices firm.

text.p: Volume on the Istabul gold exchange slipped to 903 kilos on Tuesday from Monday's 1,338 kilos on higher prices, dealers said.
Gold closed at $342.00 an ounce and 1,608,500 lira per gram, compared with $341.70 and 1,601,900 lira on Monday, following slightly firmer levels on European markets.

"With the exception of a 100-kilo arbitrage deal by one of the banks, all of the trade was due to physical demand. Bazaar traders bought gold to deliver to the state mint to cope with an expected extra demand," one dealer said.
Turkey's free gold market is concentrated around Istanbul's Grand Bazaar.
Bazaar jewellers have to bring in bullion to the state mint by Wednesday morning to have gold coins produced to sell to the public.
The Turkish currency fell to 145,720 lira to the dollar from Monday's close of 145,400 in line with a rise in the dollar/mark parity and overnight funding costs.
Most of the day's gold trade -- 813 kilos -- took place in the morning session with 81.7 percent of trade in lira terms.
